matches.rationale: No finding addresses the cherry-picked FID range (2.38–2.64) and omission of higher FIDs from the abstract. Pred_id 2 mentions a different FID range (2.15–2.38) that does not match the corrupted text.
No finding discusses the undefined L_reg or ambiguous conditioning variable c in Equation 2.
No finding points to missing hyperparameter details (clip norm, scheduler specifics, batch size clarification) in Table C.1.
No finding identifies the overstated claim in the introduction about grafting 'proving' to be lightweight and its limited testing scope.
No finding addresses the use of '✗' for FID>50 or the ambiguity of ΔFLOPs_op in Table 4.

Pred_id 1 identifies the fabricated claim that Goldschmidt [4] provides a theoretical foundation for neural network grafting, matching the same fabricated biological inspiration footnote in the introduction.

Pred_id 3 captures a direct contradiction between Section 3.4 and Figure 2 caption about the number of layers with L_k>0.5 vs. >0.7, which is the central consistency issue of the locality metric interpretation.
No finding discusses the unfair GenEval comparison (unspecified sampling steps, LoRA vs full finetuning) in the PixArt-Σ experiment.
No finding addresses the misleading comparison between the depth-to-width grafted model (712M params) and TinyDiT-D14 (340M params) without acknowledging the parameter-count disparity.

Although pred_id 5 concerns conclusion overstatement, it describes a claim that grafting 'completely solves architecture design' and 'universally outperforms', which differs from the ground truth error of omitting limitations and over-optimism in the actual conclusion text.
No finding mentions the small, unexplained batch size (2) used for latency measurement in Table 5. Pred_id 4 addresses a speedup calculation inconsistency, not the batch-size reporting issue.
No finding discusses the discrepancy between the abstract's '<2% pretraining compute' claim and the data/training-step details in the experiments.
No finding detects the insertion of promotional language ('revolutionary', 'paradigm shift') in the introduction.
No finding addresses the incorrect FLOP calculation for MHA in Appendix H.1 or the resulting inconsistency with reported ΔFLOPs_op reductions.
Pred_id 7 identifies the misrepresentation of Shen et al. [52] as prior work on operator replacement in diffusion models, matching the fabricated relevance of [52] in the related work.
